co_peg_leg_wall.blurb: Peg Leg Wall is a small sport crag in the Shelf Road canyon country north of Cañon City, on the south side of the canyon road facing the north end of The Bank's main cliffs. Sixteen routes, nearly all bolted with a single trad line, climb thin, vertical limestone with sharp edges and pockets. The spread runs from one easy-ish 5.7 up to a lone 5.13, but the bulk of it sits between 5.10 and 5.12, so this is a spot for climbers already comfortable on technical face moves. It faces northeast and stays shady, which suits warmer days, and it sees little traffic compared with its busier neighbours. Expect a short uphill hike from the road.

co_rock_of_ages.blurb: Rock of Ages is a granite crag in Rocky Mountain National Park above Estes Park, reached from the Fern Lake end of the valley. Routes mostly run one to three pitches and about 100 to 200 feet, a friendly alternative to long alpine days. The rock is fine-grained and grippy, though some patches are scaly and a few lower sections are harder to smear. The wall faces mainly south, with the dihedrals picking up shade for part of the day. Nearly everything here starts at 5.10 and climbs through the 5.11 and 5.12 range, with a few 5.13s, and most lines are trad with a handful of bolted ones. It is a destination for strong cragging climbers, not beginners.
